title: F4 Complexity Estimation over Rings Modulo q
summary: F4 extends to polynomial rings modulo q, including composite q; whether finite-field complexity estimation generalizes to this setting, and how, remains open.

formal_statement.body: The F4 algorithm has been extended to polynomial rings over the integers modulo $q$, including the setting where $q$ is composite, but it is unresolved whether the standard procedure for estimating F4 complexity over finite fields can be generalized to this ring setting. The task is to determine whether such a generalization exists and, if so, how it should estimate the complexity of F4 for polynomial systems over the integers modulo $q$.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis and Gröbner-basis complexity over polynomial rings modulo integers.
parameters: q: modulus defining the coefficient ring, potentially composite
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the standard finite-field procedure for estimating F4 complexity generalizes to polynomial rings modulo q and, if so, how to formulate the resulting estimate.

citations.label: Cryptanalysis of Symmetric Primitives over Rings and a Key Recovery Attack on Rubato

progress.summary: The paper explicitly states that it is unclear whether the typical F4 complexity-estimation procedure generalizes to polynomial rings modulo q. It reports comparative experiments but leaves a general estimation method unresolved.
citation_labels: Lorenzo Grassi et al., Cryptanalysis of Symmetric Primitives over Rings and a Key Recovery Attack on Rubato
